description:
FILED s543x (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28, base main 6a5a0631 = MAIN-READY-117 + records, v2-16900; tree v2-17200) by the list-operator first-operand batch (#5510 #5504 #5513 #5515).

THE SHAPE (neutral reproducer, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on the s543x tree):

    $| = 1; my $sh = "/bin/sh";
    my $rc = system $sh "argv0", "-c", 'echo ok';   # perl: prints ok, rc 0
    my @a = ("argv0", "-c", 'echo ok'); $rc = system $sh @a;
    PCL: PCL: statement dropped ... Missing case: ['Token::Symbol<$sh>', ...]

perl's rule is the indirect-object slot's (toke.c, case '$', the one rule s543x made PCL's `print $fh` and
`sort $by` ask: `Pl::PExpr::_is_scalar_fh_token` + `_is_print_term_start`); PCL has the slot for print / printf / say
/ sort and the BLOCK form of system / exec (`indirect_program`, #2082) but no scalar arm for system / exec.  The fix
is the block arm's node (`indirect_program`) built from a scalar when the slot predicate says so.
frequency_reason: grep over the wide list, the board dists, everyday, lib/ and the Rosetta corpus (s543x): 0 sites; perlfunc teaches it
subject: DROP (rare): `system $prog LIST` / `exec $prog LIST` -- a SCALAR indirect object (perlfunc exec's own `exec $shell '-sh'` example) is a dropped statement ("Bug. Fell through"); the block form `system { $prog } LIST` works
triage_reason: the indirect-object PROGRAM of system / exec is documented core syntax (perlfunc exec); IN by docs/supported-subset.md section 3
